Signer usage guidance: Define a shared signer, then reference its name in a CA's advanced configuration (crlSignerName) to sign CRLs. The CA's certificate signing key is configured separately.
Requestor usage guidance: Identify an external XiPKI client by its certificate, then bind it to a CA with permitted operations and certificate profiles. Web accounts and roles are managed separately.
Publisher usage guidance: Define a publisher, then bind it to a CA to publish subsequent certificate and revocation changes. To publish existing certificates, use Republish Certificates in System Management.
PKCS12 signer type description: Read a software signing key and certificate from a PKCS#12 keystore.
JCEKS signer type description: Read a software signing key and certificate from a JCEKS keystore.
PKCS11 signer type description: Use a key in an HSM or other PKCS#11 token already configured in the CA.
Certificate requestor type description: cert is the requestor type supported by this XiPKI runtime. Configuration contains the client's X.509 certificate, encoded as Base64 DER.
OCSP publisher type description: Publish certificate status to a XiPKI OCSP database. This does not start an OCSP HTTP responder.
File signer example guidance: Replace CHANGE_ME, the path and key-label with your keystore password, CA-container file path and private-key alias. algo must match the key; parallelism=2 creates two concurrent signers. The certificate field may be empty when it is available in the keystore.
Hardware signer example guidance: Replace module and the key label with configured values. Specify exactly one of slot (zero-based index) or slot-id, and exactly one of key-label or key-id. The token PIN belongs in the CA's PKCS#11 configuration. Supply the matching signing certificate in the Base64 certificate field; CRL signing requires cRLSign key usage.
Certificate requestor example guidance: This abbreviated example cannot be submitted as a real certificate. Paste the complete Base64 content between BEGIN CERTIFICATE and END CERTIFICATE from your client certificate, without the PEM markers. Do not enter a CSR or private key.
OCSP publisher example guidance: Replace YOUR_OCSP_DATASOURCE with the name of an OCSP datasource already registered in the CA configuration. publish.goodcerts=true publishes valid certificates as well as revoked ones; false publishes revoked certificates only. A Web database connection is not an OCSP datasource.
